Subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets (Finex discovery)

Hi Alex

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size throughput and propose an initial Dedicated/Hosted plan:

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workload: document summarization + assistant UI for customers
- Target model family: open Llama-3 variants (you mentioned 70B for long form and 13B for assistant)
- Key SLOs you called out: p95 user-facing latency target around 200-300ms for short interactions, streaming for progressive tokens is desirable for UX

What we need to size throughput (please confirm or correct):
1) Typical tokens per request (distribution): short vs medium vs long. Example: mean tokens, 95th percentile tokens, and absolute max you expect.
2) Expected steady-state QPS / concurrency and peak burst QPS. If you have hourly or daily percentiles (p50/p95/p99) that helps.
3) Whether streaming is required for all requests or just the short/assistant flows. Streaming changes resource planning.
4) Any hard latency SLOs (e.g., p95 <= 200ms) and whether you can tolerate graceful degradation (e.g., fallback to smaller model for spikes).

Next steps / ask from you
- Can you share a sample traffic file (tokens per request + timestamp) for the last 7-30 days? A CSV with columns: timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_type is perfect.
- Confirm whether peak bursts are expected (e.g., product launches) and how long they last (minutes/hours).
- Preferred time for a technical deep-dive (30-45m) next week to go over workload patterns and our proposed GPU footprint.

Rough guidance (so you have a baseline)
- Mapping tokens/sec to GPU throughput: a 4x speed difference between 13B/70B depending on quant/optimizations; we'll run an internal calc once we get your distribution.
- Streaming: if you need <200ms p95 with streaming, we typically recommend reserved Dedicated capacity to avoid cold-start variability.

Attachments: None from our side yet if you can send the CSV, we'll produce a throughput spreadsheet and propose instance counts.

Thanks
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Hi Rafael

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few data points and attaching a 7-day export (finex_sample_traffic.csv). High level:

Traffic breakdown (last 7 days)
- Short/assistant interactions: ~70% of requests, median tokens ~45 (in+out), p95 ~120
- Medium requests (summaries of 5-10 pages): ~25% of requests, median tokens ~260, p95 ~520
- Long batch jobs (document ingestion + long-form summarization): ~5% of requests, tokens range 2k-5k, max ~6k

QPS / concurrency
- Steady-state: ~15-25 QPS (mostly short interactions), typical concurrency ~30 sessions actively using assistant
- Peak bursts: up to ~120 QPS for short windows (5-20 minutes) during peak business hours or feature experiments

Latency SLOs and streaming
- UX goal: p95 <= 300ms for assistant (short interactions); for medium/long jobs we accept higher latency but want progress streaming for the medium ones.
- Streaming: desirable for assistant flows. Long batch jobs can be async.

Other notes
- We can share 30 days if useful but redacted; starting with 7-day sample to keep things simple.
- Interested in a cost estimate and recommended Dedicated sizing assuming 3x growth over 12 months.

Attached: finex_sample_traffic.csv (7-day export).

Thanks

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets (Finex discovery)

Alex

Appreciate the data, this is exactly what we need. I pulled the CSV and ran a quick pass to translate into tokens/sec and estimated GPU footprint, attaching a starter calc (redwood_throughput_calc.xlsx). Key takeaways from the quick pass:

1) Baseline steady-state throughput
- Using your steady-state 20 QPS and ~45 tokens/request for short interactions => ~900 tokens/sec of short workload. Adding medium requests (25% at 260 tokens) brings steady-state to ~2.8k tokens/sec.

2) Peak sizing (burst protection)
- Peak short-only bursts at 120 QPS => 120 * 45 = 5.4k tokens/sec for short flows. If a simultaneous medium job batch runs during a peak, peak tokens/sec could reach ~8-9k.

3) Mapping to GPU counts (very rough initial)
- For a quantized 13B optimized runtime we typically see ~50-70k tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and kv-cache behavior; for 70B the per-GPU throughput is ~8-12k tokens/sec.
- Given that, your steady-state (~2.8k tokens/sec) fits easily on a single 70B-optimized GPU for latency-sensitive paths, but peaks (8-9k tokens/sec) imply either:
  a) Dedicated provision for 1+ 70B GPUs with autoscale to add 1-2 GPUs for bursts, or
  b) Route medium/long jobs to a separate queued batch tier (async) while keeping assistant traffic on reserved capacity.

4) Streaming implications
- Streaming for short assistant flows tends to reduce perceived latency but increases scheduling pressure (many small incremental responses). We recommend reserving capacity for assistant streaming to meet p95 targets.

Questions / asks
- Can you confirm which model(s) you'd like to prioritize for p95 targets (13B assistant, 70B long-form)? That changes the per-GPU numbers.
- Expected growth: you mentioned 3x in 12 months — can you confirm timeline (linear growth vs step changes tied to releases)?

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive (45m) to align on model variants, streaming patterns, and final throughput spreadsheet.
- We'll include cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated and a recommended config for burst protection and async routing.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite. Marissa, can you help propose 2 slots?

Thanks
Rafael

Attachment: redwood_throughput_calc.xlsx
